consequences.text: If the developer has turned on data sharing or linked an ads account, Google may use this data for its own products and personalized ads. FinePrint can't see that setting. This code also ships inside Google's ads SDK, so finding it doesn't show the developer uses Analytics.

consequences.text: In 2025 a US federal jury found Google liable for invading the privacy of people who had turned off Web & App Activity. Their activity in other companies' apps still reached Google, through its Firebase or Google Mobile Ads code. Judgment for about $425.7 million was entered in 2026. Google has appealed.
consequences.wording: Decided by a jury in a US federal court (verdict 2025-09-03, judgment 2026-03-02); under appeal.

procedural_note.text: The court denied Google's renewed motion for judgment as a matter of law on 2026-08-28. Google appealed to the Ninth Circuit on 2026-09-21 (No. 26-6237); the plaintiffs filed a conditional cross-appeal on 2026-10-05.

sources.title: Rodriguez v. Google LLC (N.D. Cal. No. 3:20-cv-04688), order denying the renewed motions for judgment as a matter of law
sources.quote: For the reasons set forth below, both motions are denied.

sources.title: Rodriguez v. Google LLC (N.D. Cal. No. 3:20-cv-04688), final judgment

sources.quote: whose activity on a non-Google-branded mobile app was still transmitted to Google … because of the Firebase Software Development Kit (“SDK”) and/or Google Mobile Ads SDK
